messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• Texas law allows local governments to set lower limits on state‑maintained roads if they meet certain criteria. | Speed limits are posted; drivers must obey them. | | **Seat Belt Use** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Failure to buckle up can result in a fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Handheld cell phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a fine and points. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%). | Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• Give right‑of‑way to emergency vehicles with flashing lights. | Failure to yield can lead to citations and liability. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Do not drive in the left lane on highways unless overtaking. | Improper lane usage can result in a ticket. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for school buses when they display flashing red lights and extend a stop sign.
• Vehicles must stop regardless of direction. | Violations are heavily fined. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in no‑stop zones, fire lanes, or handicap spaces without proper permits.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited unless marked otherwise. | Violations can lead to towing and fines. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Must have working headlights, taillights, brake lights, turn signals, and horn.
• Mirrors must be present and properly adjusted. | Failure to comply can result in a citation. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Driving without insurance is a felony. | | **Points System** | • Traffic violations accrue points on the driver’s record.
• Accumulating 12 points within 36 months can lead to license suspension. | Points are tracked by the Texas Department of Public Safety. | ### How to Find Specific Laws - **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic regulations. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Offers guides, FAQs, and updates on enforcement. - **Local County Ordinances** – May impose additional restrictions (e.g., speed limits, parking rules). ### Resources - [Texas DPS Traffic Law Guide](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/traffic-laws) - [Texas Transportation Code](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/) - [Texas DPS License Suspension & Points](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/license-suspension-points) Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific rule or how to handle a particular situation!
